content.title: About
content.content: Guisada is a traditional Mexican stew made with slow‑cooked beef in a sauce of tomatoes, chilies, spices and aromatic herbs. The meat becomes tender while the sauce develops a rich, slightly spicy and fragrant flavor.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Guisada is often prepared in clay pots (cazuelas), which enhance the aroma.
Classic recipes include bay leaves and cinnamon, giving the dish its characteristic Mexican scent.
The dish is especially popular in the Yucatán and Oaxaca regions, where it is served with corn tortillas.
In some areas guisada is accompanied by rice, beans and a squeeze of lime.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: Beef provides all essential amino acids needed for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Iron and zinc
items.content: Beef is a good source of heme iron and zinc, supporting immunity and energy metabolism.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Guisada supplies vitamin B12, niacin and riboflavin, important for the nervous system and metabolism.

items.title: Low in carbohydrates
items.content: The dish fits low‑carb diets because its calories come mainly from protein and fat.

items.title: Beneficial plant compounds
items.content: Tomatoes, chilies and spices add antioxidants such as lycopene and capsaicin.

items.title: High saturated fat content
items.content: Slow‑cooked beef can contain notable amounts of saturated fat; people with heart disease should watch portion size.

items.title: Sodium level
items.content: The sauce often includes added salt or soy sauce, raising the sodium content.

items.title: Spice allergy
items.content: Some individuals may be allergic to chilies, coriander or cumin.

items.title: Digestive heaviness
items.content: Rich meat can be heavy on the stomach for those with sensitive digestion.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve hot guisada with tortillas, rice or corn grits. Add fresh lime juice, cilantro and sliced avocado for extra brightness.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep cooked guisada in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. For longer storage, freeze portions for up to 2 months. Reheat thoroughly before serving.
